# Results (generated by `python -m llm_router evaluate`; never edited by hand)

- Small tier: `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` ($0.1/1M in, $0.4/1M out)
- Large tier: `gemini-3.8-flash` ($0.75/1M in, $3.75/1M out)
- Questions: 404 usable (0 dropped for missing outcomes); train 202 / held-out test 202, stratified by source
- Quality is exact match (number or letter). No LLM judge. Intervals are 95% paired bootstrap over test questions

## Summary (computed from the numbers below)

- **Headroom exists.** Small model accuracy 0.916, large 0.985; the small model costs 18% of the large model per request.
- **Routing could pay off in principle.** An oracle that escalates only when the small model fails reaches accuracy 0.990 at 29% of the large model's cost, escalating 8% of questions.
- **The routers did not capture it.** The pre-fixed learned router (learned@0.9) escalated 14% and was indistinguishable from a random mix; its ROC-AUC shows no detectable skill (interval includes 0.5).

## Headroom: how much better is the large model?

| source | n | small acc | large acc |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k | 200 | 0.935 | 0.975 |
| mmlu | 204 | 0.902 | 0.985 |

Rows collapsed because their routing decisions were identical to another row: learned@0.5, learned@0.7, learned@0.8 (identical to always_small); learned@0.95 (identical to always_large). The learned router's scores on the test set ranged only from 0.83 to 0.95, so the threshold sweep carries little information. The full table is in `results/summary.json`.

## Headline operating point: learned@0.9 (fixed before looking at held-out results)

- Routed 14% of test questions to the large model.
- Accuracy 0.936 [0.901, 0.965] versus always-large 0.985 [0.965, 1.000]; the paired difference -0.050 [-0.084, -0.020] is below zero at 95%.
- Cost was 26.6 [20.0, 34.3] % of always-large.
- Versus a random mix sending the same 14% to the large model, accuracy differs by 0.010 [-0.005, 0.029], which is not distinguishable from zero. This is the test of whether the router has real skill.

## Exploratory diagnostics (added AFTER seeing the headline result; not pre-specified)

Small-model failures: 16 in the training half, 17 in the test half. Few failures means little signal to learn from and wide intervals.

## Router overhead (this machine, per request, single prompt)

- rules: 0.008 ms; learned (embedding + logistic regression): 10.0 ms

## Limitations

- Small benchmark (hundreds of questions), two model tiers from one provider, and a replay evaluation: each question was run once per tier, and policies are scored on those recorded outcomes.
- Latencies come from the collection run under 8-way concurrency, so they include some contention. They are not a load test.
- Only exact-match tasks (math and multiple choice). Results may not transfer to open-ended or conversational traffic.
- Several thresholds are shown for context; only the headline threshold was fixed in advance.
- Prices are list prices copied into `config.yaml` on the date noted there. Costs scale with them.
